enonce_intro_markdown: A golf player hits a ball from a point $O$ on horizontal ground with a velocity of $v\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ [printed in the scan as a root sign with the number 13] at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal, where $\tan\theta =$ [value missing in the scan]. The ball first hits the ground at a point $A$, where $OA = 120\ \mathrm m$. (Take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.)
incertitudes: Question 3 : l'énoncé imprime « a velocity of [racine 13] m s^-1 » (un signe de racine avec un petit v en indice) et « tan theta = » sans valeur. On lit v comme l'inconnue de (a) ; v et tan theta sont retrouvés à partir de OA = 120 m et du résultat imprimé de (b) (v sin theta = 30) : tan theta = 3/2 et v = 10 racine(13) m/s, cohérent avec le « 13 » imprimé.
Question 3 : le sujet imprime « Take g as 10 m s^-2 » (valeur retenue g = 10). Les mots « The bail » (coquille de « ball ») sont lus « ball ».

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model.** Projectile motion under gravity only ($g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, printed on the paper). Take $O$ as origin, $x$ horizontal towards $A$, $y$ vertically upwards. Components of the initial velocity: $u_x = v\cos\theta$, $u_y = v\sin\theta$.

The ball returns to the ground at the time $T$ with $0 = u_yT - \tfrac12 gT^2$, so $T = \dfrac{2u_y}{g}$. The range is

$$OA = u_x T = \frac{2u_xu_y}{g} = 120 \;\Rightarrow\; u_xu_y = 600$$

The printed result of part (b) ($h = 30t - 5t^2$) gives $u_y = 30\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, hence $u_x = 600/30 = 20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and

$$\tan\theta = \frac{30}{20} = \frac32,\qquad v = \sqrt{20^2 + 30^2} = \sqrt{1300} = 10\sqrt{13}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}} \approx 36.1\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

(Check with the formula $R = \dfrac{v^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$: $\tan\theta = \tfrac32$ gives $\sin2\theta = \dfrac{2\tan\theta}{1 + \tan^2\theta} = \dfrac{3}{13/4} = \dfrac{12}{13}$, so $R = \dfrac{1300\times 12/13}{10} = 120\ \mathrm m$. The number $13$ under the root sign printed in the statement is consistent with this.)

**$v = 10\sqrt{13} \approx 36.1\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, with $\tan\theta = \tfrac32$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that its height $h$ above the ground at time $t$ seconds is given by $h = (30t - 5t^2)\ \mathrm m$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Vertical motion with constant acceleration $-g = -10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ and initial vertical velocity $u_y = v\sin\theta$. With $\tan\theta = \tfrac32$: $\sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{13}}$, so

$$u_y = 10\sqrt{13}\times\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} = 30\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

Using $h = u_yt - \tfrac12 gt^2$:

$$h = 30t - \tfrac12(10)t^2 = 30t - 5t^2\ \mathrm m$$

**Hence $h = (30t - 5t^2)\ \mathrm m$, as required.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Hence, or otherwise, find the maximum height reached by the ball above the level of projection.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The maximum height occurs when the vertical velocity is zero:

$$\frac{dh}{dt} = 30 - 10t = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; t = 3\ \mathrm s$$

$$h_{max} = 30(3) - 5(3)^2 = 90 - 45 = 45\ \mathrm m$$

(Check: $u_y^2 = 2gh_{max} \Rightarrow 900 = 20h_{max} \Rightarrow h_{max} = 45\ \mathrm m$.)

**Maximum height $= 45\ \mathrm m$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Hence, or otherwise, find the time of flight.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The ball is back on the ground when $h = 0$:

$$30t - 5t^2 = 5t(6 - t) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; t = 0\ \text{(launch)}\ \text{or}\ t = 6$$

**Time of flight $= 6\ \mathrm s$.** (Check: $u_xT = 20\times 6 = 120\ \mathrm m = OA$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Hence, or otherwise, find the Cartesian equation of the trajectory of the ball.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Horizontal motion at constant velocity $u_x = 20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$: $x = 20t$, so $t = \dfrac{x}{20}$. Vertical position: $y = 30t - 5t^2$. Eliminate $t$:

$$y = 30\cdot\frac{x}{20} - 5\cdot\frac{x^2}{400} = \frac{3x}{2} - \frac{x^2}{80}$$

**Cartesian equation: $y = \dfrac{3}{2}x - \dfrac{x^2}{80}$** (with $x$ and $y$ in metres, $0 \le x \le 120$).

(Check: $y = 0$ at $x = 0$ and $x = 120$; the maximum is at $x = 60$, where $y = 90 - 45 = 45\ \mathrm m$. This also equals $x\tan\theta - \dfrac{gx^2}{2v^2\cos^2\theta}$ with $\tan\theta = \tfrac32$, $v^2\cos^2\theta = 400$.)
